brief: Bad vs Good vs Great pricing — 6 patterns that separate $99 from $9,900 offers.

slots.body: Bad freelancers charge by the hour, punishing efficiency. Good creators sell fixed projects. Great consultants price against the revenue or cost savings they generate.
slots.note: If your client wins big, you win big. Tie your fee to their upside.

slots.body: Bad offers say 'no refunds.' Good ones include a 30-day guarantee. Great deals offer conditional assurances that only trigger if milestones are missed.
slots.note: A strong guarantee signals confidence and filters serious buyers.

slots.body: Bad agencies serve everyone. Good shops focus on one industry. Great firms define an entirely new category where they are the only logical choice.
slots.note: Specialization removes price comparison. You become the benchmark.

slots.body: Bad proposals rely on vague promises. Good sellers share testimonials. Great leaders present case studies with exact metrics, timelines, and client names.
slots.note: Specific proof justifies specific prices. Vague claims attract haggling.

slots.body: Bad menus list ten options. Good sellers use three tiers. Great advisors design one bespoke package that feels irreplaceable and scarce.
slots.note: Scarcity and customization support premium positioning better than discounts.

slots.body: Bad sellers take any call. Good consultants use a qualification form. Great experts charge for a diagnostic audit that converts into the main engagement.
slots.note: A paid discovery call proves budget exists and establishes your expertise.

slots.body: Pick one tactic and implement it this week. Small shifts in positioning create massive jumps in profit.
